CuH-catalyzed stereoselective desymmetrization
of prochiral cyclopentane-1,3-diones
via alkoxyallylation
Sundaram Maurya,†<sup>ab</sup> Vaibhav B. Patil,†<sup>a</sup> G. Raghu Ramudu,<sup>ab</sup> Virendra S. Amrutkar,<sup>a</sup>
Yash G. Mendapara,<sup>a</sup> Jagadeesh Babu Nanubolu <sup>bc</sup> and Rambabu Chegondi
ab
We report a CuH-catalyzed enantioselective desymmetrization of
prochiral 2,2-disubstituted cyclopentane-1,3-diones through reduc-
tive alkoxyallylation. This strategy exploits the carbonyl group, an
underexplored reactivity mode for the desymmetrization of
cyclopentane-1,3-diones, constructing complex chiral carbocycles
from simple symmetric diketones. This eficient, atom-economic
transformation delivers functionalized cyclopentanones, bearing
three consecutive stereocenters, including two quaternary carbons
in a single operation. The protocol exhibits broad substrate scope,
high diastereoselectivity, and moderate to good enantioselectivity.
The allylation of carbonyl compounds using allylmetal reagents to
synthesize tertiary homoallylic alcohols has been extensively stu-
died and developed over the past several decades.<sup>1</sup> Furthermore,
the use of chiral catalysts in allylations allows for precise control
over the stereochemistry of the resulting products.<sup>2</sup> Despite several
advances, the application of such strategies to ketones remains
challenging due to their lower reactivity compared to aldehydes.<sup>3</sup>
Traditional allylmetal reagents used for ketone allylations<sup>4–9</sup> are
often harsh and sensitive, used in stoichiometric amounts, leading
to challenges in chemoselectivity, exothermicity, and enantioselec-
tivity, which restrict their suitability for large-scale applications.
Nonetheless, the emergence of transition-metal catalyzed in situ-
generated allylmetal nucleophiles from allene, 1,3-diene or alkyne
pronucleophiles for carbonyl allylation has emerged as a mild,
versatile, and highly effective strategy that eliminates the need for
generating stoichiometric metal waste, a concept originally devel-
oped by Krische.<sup>10</sup> In particular, allylation of ketones using
the cost-effective CuH-catalysis has proven to be a powerful
approach, enabling the coupling of ketones with diverse allyl
pronucleophiles.<sup>11</sup> In this approach, allenes and diene-derived
nucleophiles serve as allyl anion equivalents in combination with
a silyl hydride reductant, enabling the synthesis of homoallylic
alcohols in high enantio- and diastereoselectivity. Notable contri-
butions to advancements in this area have been made by
Buchwald,<sup>11a,12a–d</sup> Sieber,<sup>12e–h</sup> and others,<sup>12i</sup> commonly using var-
ious substituted allenes to afford highly-functionalized chiral
homoallylic alcohols and amines. However, achieving enantio-
selective allylation under these conditions presents significant
challenges, viz., alkene isomerization in the presence of base
and the risk of direct reduction of any ketone moiety in the
substrate caused by the highly reactive CuH-complex.<sup>13</sup> Building
upon our prior work in Cu-catalyzed transformations,<sup>14</sup> we devel-
oped CuH-catalyzed allylation of ketones using alkoxyallenes<sup>15</sup> to
access highly functionalized syn-tert,sec-1,2-diols with excellent
yields and stereoselectivity (Scheme 1b).<sup>14c</sup>
Desymmetrization, a privileged strategy in organic synth-
esis, enables the conversion of symmetric, often readily avail-
able scafolds into complex, chiral architectures with high
stereoselectivity in a single step. Our group also developed a
cost-efective and eficient enantioselective CuH-catalyzed
desymmetrization of cyclopentane-1,3-diones (Scheme 1b).<sup>14a</sup>
Notably, the desymmetrization of cyclic 1,3-diones via substitu-
tions on the carbocyclic ring via conjugate additions, cycload-
dition, C(sp<sup>2</sup>)–H functionalizations, etc., has been studied in
detail so far.<sup>16</sup> In contrast, fewer desymmetrization reports exist
on exploiting the carbonyl group (Scheme 1a).<sup>17</sup> Motivated by
our interest in the desymmetrization of cyclic 1,3-diones,<sup>16d,18</sup>
we report the first enantioselective CuH-catalyzed reductive
alkoxyallylation of 2,2-disubstituted cyclopentane-1,3-diones
generating highly-functionalized pentacycles (Scheme 1c). This
reaction probably proceeds through the formation of a kineti-
cally favorable ‘open’ Z-selective s-allylcopper complex<sup>14c</sup>
undergoing coupling with the cyclic 1,3-dione via a six-
membered cyclic allylcopper complex TS-1. This economical
method provides highly functionalized cyclopentanones

Based on the literature reports<sup>21</sup> and our previous obser-
vations,<sup>14a,c,d</sup> the probable mechanistic cycle of Cu(I)-catalyzed
reductive coupling of alkoxyallene with cyclic 1,3-diones has
been proposed in Scheme 3. Firstly, a copper-hydride complex A
generates in situ from the copper-salt, bisphosphine ligand,
LiO<sup>t</sup>Bu, and PMHS. The alkoxyallene 2a undergoes addition of
a BINAP-CuH-complex, providing a transient, kinetically favor-
able ‘open’ Z-selective s-allyl Cu complex
\mathbf { B } , ^ { 1 4 c }
to readily
undergo nucleophilic addition to 1a through a closed six-
membered cyclic transition state C, to generate the Cu–oxide
complex D. Lastly, metathesis of complex D with PMHS regen-
erates the CuH-complex A, while lithium exchange and acidic
workup releases the product 3a.
In summary, this work describes the stereoselective CuH-
catalyzed reductive allylation of 2,2-disubstituted cyclopentane-
1,3-diones. This method provides highly functionalized pentacyc-
lic products containing three contiguous stereocentres, with two
quaternary carbon centers, including an all-carbon quaternary
carbon center. The reaction proceeds well with diverse substrates
in good to high yields and high diastereoselectivities. A scale-up
reaction along with further elaborations on the products was
conducted to demonstrate the utility of the method.

Based on the literature reports<sup>21</sup> and our previous obser-
vations,<sup>14a,c,d</sup> the probable mechanistic cycle of Cu(I)-catalyzed
reductive coupling of alkoxyallene with cyclic 1,3-diones has
been proposed in Scheme 3. Firstly, a copper-hydride complex A
generates in situ from the copper-salt, bisphosphine ligand,
LiO<sup>t</sup>Bu, and PMHS. The alkoxyallene 2a undergoes addition of
a BINAP-CuH-complex, providing a transient, kinetically favor-
able ‘open’ Z-selective s-allyl Cu complex
\mathbf { B } , ^ { 1 4 c }
to readily
undergo nucleophilic addition to 1a through a closed six-
membered cyclic transition state C, to generate the Cu–oxide
complex D. Lastly, metathesis of complex D with PMHS regen-
erates the CuH-complex A, while lithium exchange and acidic
workup releases the product 3a.
In summary, this work describes the stereoselective CuH-
catalyzed reductive allylation of 2,2-disubstituted cyclopentane-
1,3-diones. This method provides highly functionalized pentacyc-
lic products containing three contiguous stereocentres, with two
quaternary carbon centers, including an all-carbon quaternary
carbon center. The reaction proceeds well with diverse substrates
in good to high yields and high diastereoselectivities. A scale-up
reaction along with further elaborations on the products was
conducted to demonstrate the utility of the method.
